did_you_know.text: Did you know? In Isaiah 45, Cyrus is called “my anointed one”—that is, someone chosen for a particular role—and is promised success in subduing nations and opening gates.
Did you know? The description of Cyrus’s mission includes breaking “doors of bronze” and cutting through “bars of iron,” a vivid picture emphasizing the Lord’s power to open blocked paths before him.

Did you know? The hidden treasures given to Cyrus are presented not merely as wealth, but as a means for him to know that the Lord is the one calling him by name—even though Cyrus himself does not know the Lord.
Did you know? According to the chapter, Cyrus is chosen “for the sake of my servant Jacob” and Israel, even though Cyrus does not know the identity of the God directing his mission.
Did you know? One of the chapter’s central ideas is God’s exclusivity: “I am the Lord, and there is no other; besides me there is no God”—a statement repeated in several forms throughout the chapter.

Did you know? The verse “I form light and create darkness, I make peace and create evil” presents the Lord as sovereign over every realm of reality; in the biblical context, “evil” can also refer to calamity or disaster.

Did you know? In verse 8, righteousness and salvation are portrayed as springing up from the earth after the heavens pour down righteousness—a poetic combination of natural imagery with moral and divine rule.

Did you know? The metaphor of the clay and the potter teaches that the created being cannot rebel against its maker or demand an account of his actions, just as clay cannot instruct the one who shapes it.

Did you know? The chapter attributes Cyrus’s rise “in righteousness” to the Lord, along with his mission to rebuild the Lord’s city and release the exiles, emphasizing that the release will be “not for price or a bribe.”

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, the invitation to salvation is extended to “all the ends of the earth”: all nations are called to turn to the Lord, and it is then declared that every knee will bow and every tongue will swear allegiance to him.
